stem: Two scouting rounds each record 3 affected plants, but the first round inspected 30 plants and the second inspected 120. What is the best interpretation?
choices: The raw counts are not directly comparable as incidence until the different sampling denominators are accounted for.
The pressure is unchanged because both rounds found exactly 3 affected plants.
The second round proves severity decreased because more plants were inspected.
Only the latest raw count should be retained because it used the larger sample.
rationale: Comparable scouting requires the sampling denominator and method context; equal raw counts can represent different incidence when sampling effort differs.
